clue.text: Sporting equipment used by member of one

definitions.text: Sporting equipment used by member of one

parts.words: Sporting equipment used by member of one
parts.note: the stick a golfer swings shares its name with the society the golfer belongs to, so the item is used by a member of one of itself

explanation.surface: A piece of kit carried by someone who belongs to an association.
explanation.walkthrough: The name means both the iron or wood a golfer swings and the association of golfers; 'one' points back to the same two words in their second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The stick used to hit the ball in golf is used by people who belong to a society of golfers sharing that name.

clue.text: Bird that's extremely comical with head invisible

indicators.note: the first letter of the built word is made to vanish, as though its head were out of sight

parts.note: extremely means most, as in 'most kind'
rich means laughable or absurd, as in 'that's rich'

explanation.surface: A bird that is hilarious and buries its head out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with head invisible' removes the M from MOSTRICH. The surface nods to the belief that this bird hides its head in the sand.
explanation.definitionFit: The large flightless African runner is a species of bird.

clue.text: Dismiss Ibsen hero as agitator

parts.note: to dismiss from a job is to fire
Brand is the title hero of Henrik Ibsen's verse drama

explanation.surface: Sack the Norwegian playwright's protagonist for stirring up trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A troublemaker who stirs up unrest is called by this word for a burning torch.

clue.text: Deliberately took some of Polonius's advice?

definitions.meaning: slowly, in the musical direction for a slow tempo
Polonius in Hamlet says 'neither a borrower nor a lender be'; someone who lent nothing, written as lent plus O for nought, followed half of it

explanation.surface: Someone consciously followed part of the old courtier's counsel.
explanation.walkthrough: Polonius, in Shakespeare's Hamlet, advises 'Neither a borrower nor a lender be': having LENT O (nothing) obeys the lender half.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the Italian tempo marking means slowly, in an unhurried, deliberate way.

clue.text: New Age gift

parts.note: read 'new age' as the start of a further year of a person's life, and the gift is the one given on that day

explanation.surface: A crystal or incense offering from the alternative-spirituality movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Age' suggests crystals and mysticism; it means simply turning a year older.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift marking the anniversary of someone's arrival in the world comes as they reach a new age.

clue.text: Native American quickly swallowing hard

indicators.note: one word takes the other inside it, as a mouth takes in food

parts.note: apace means quickly
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An indigenous American gulps down something tough at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowing' puts H inside APACE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache are a group of Indigenous peoples of the American Southwest.

clue.text: Off course over an hour — smoking remains found here

indicators.note: in a down clue one word sits over and around another, so the first holds the second

parts.note: astray means off course, wandering
H is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: A ship wandered off course for an hour, and the evidence of someone smoking turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts H inside ASTRAY. 'smoking remains' reads as smouldering wreckage but means a smoker's ash.
explanation.definitionFit: Cigarette ash and stubs, the leftovers of smoking, are deposited in this dish.

clue.text: One of our bases in operation

parts.note: one means a, the indefinite article
a foot is one of the two bases a person stands on

explanation.surface: One of our military bases is now operational.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bases' suggests military installations; it means what we stand on.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is underway or in progress is said to be going on.

clue.text: Worker; boy, manually experienced

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as a farmhand
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A labourer's lad has practical experience.
explanation.definitionFit: Practical, done with one's own hands, describes direct physical experience of a task.

clue.text: Top player making mark on horse

definitions.meaning: the leading performer in a team or cast
the white patch on a horse's forehead

explanation.surface: The best player leaves a mark on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity performer and the white blaze on a horse's brow share this name.

clue.text: Jump on player at bridge crossing Scottish border, perhaps

indicators.note: one word is placed on top of the other, in front of it in the answer

parts.note: North is one of the four players in the card game bridge
to bound is to jump

explanation.surface: A leap on a bridge crossing over into Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' suggests a structure over a border river; it is the card game, whose players are named North, South, East and West. Crossing from England into Scotland is heading north.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling from England into Scotland means heading towards the pole, an example of moving in that direction.

clue.text: Older relative as despot in yearbook

definitions.meaning: the all-seeing ruler in Orwell's novel titled with a year, Nineteen Eighty-Four

explanation.surface: An elder sibling shown as a tyrant in the school annual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yearbook' suggests a school annual; it means a book named after a year, Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder male sibling, and the dictator figure of Orwell's dystopian novel.

clue.text: Time to seek for job

parts.note: to ask is to seek, as in asking for help

explanation.surface: Time to go looking for work.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of work to be done is a chore or assignment.

clue.text: For each person, it's in the future

parts.note: a means for each, as in 'ten pounds a ticket'
a head is a person, as in 'per head'

explanation.surface: Each individual has a future.
explanation.definitionFit: Something still to come lies forward in time, before us.

clue.text: Instrument new parents are happy to hear

definitions.text: Instrument new parents are happy to hear

parts.words: Instrument new parents are happy to hear
parts.note: the small piano's name splits into an infant and a word for splendid, what proud parents like to hear of their new child

explanation.surface: Proud parents enjoy the sound of a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The instrument is a small piano; split, its name praises a newborn as 'baby grand', which new parents are glad to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: A short horizontal piano whose name, split in two, calls an infant splendid.

clue.text: Hateful type, terribly satirical

indicators.note: terribly suggests these letters are badly mangled and must be reordered

explanation.surface: A nasty character who is dreadfully mocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges SATIRICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who holds bigoted views about ethnic groups is a hate-filled bigot.

clue.text: Oil, perhaps, comes ashore by headland

parts.note: a ship or passenger lands on coming ashore
a cape is a headland

explanation.surface: Fuel washes up on the coast beside a promontory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil' looks like the petroleum washing ashore; it is an oil painting, an example of the genre.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil painting may be an example of a picture of countryside scenery.

clue.text: Awfully bad sign in part of body

indicators.note: awfully signals that the next word's letters are messed up

parts.note: an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: A dreadful portent appears somewhere on the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' rearranges BAD to ABD.
explanation.definitionFit: The belly is the region of the body between chest and pelvis.

clue.text: Initially copied a couple of bishops in style of Biblical interpretation

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the next word

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, so two of them give BB
a la is French for in the style of

explanation.surface: A pair of clergymen first imitated a way of reading Scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Kabbalah is the Jewish mystical tradition of interpreting the Hebrew scriptures.

clue.text: Music of the 20s

definitions.meaning: written music, as in an orchestral part
the clue's plural stands for twenty as a unit

explanation.surface: The music of the Jazz Age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the 20s' suggests the decade 1920 to 1929; it means the number twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: A written musical composition is called by the same old word for a group of twenty.

clue.text: Couples finally abandoning ripe cottage cheese

indicators.note: a couple of letters at the end of each word is dropped, so the last pair of each goes

explanation.surface: Pairs of lovers move out of a run-down rural cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couples finally abandoning' drops the final two letters of RIPE and of COTTAGE, PE and GE. 'cottage cheese' is a red herring split across the parse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft Italian whey cheese.

clue.text: Aim to emerge from hideaway

indicators.note: the letters appear from within the following word

explanation.surface: Trying to get out of a secret retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: An intention or purpose is a plan in the mind.

clue.text: Sect for which America is home, primarily

parts.note: AM is an abbreviation for America or American

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A religious group whose homeland is the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes H from 'home'; 'for which' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amish are a traditionalist Anabaptist Christian community.

clue.text: Braced a knee almost damaged in acrobatic performance

indicators.note: damaged signals the letters are broken up and reassembled
almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: A dancer straps up a knee that's nearly wrecked mid-stunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims KNEE to KNE, and 'damaged' rearranges BRACED A KNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Street dancing with spins and acrobatic moves on the floor is a gymnastic show.

clue.text: Start off drawing boat

indicators.note: the start of the word is taken off

parts.note: a sketch is a drawing

explanation.surface: Begin making a drawing of a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start off' looks like 'begin'; it removes the S from SKETCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-masted sailing vessel is a type of boat.

clue.text: With mixed feelings, going round, about girl

indicators.note: the first word goes round the second, enclosing it

parts.note: ambient means surrounding, all about
Val is a girl's name, short for Valerie

explanation.surface: Unsure how one feels, circling a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' puts VAL inside AMBIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being torn between contradictory emotions is having mixed feelings.

clue.text: Nine of our letters returned, and one from elsewhere

definitions.text: Nine of our letters returned, and one from elsewhere

parts.words: Nine of our letters returned, and one from elsewhere
parts.note: our ninth letter, I, given in return for the matching ninth letter of the Greek alphabet, a letter from elsewhere

explanation.surface: Nine English letters come back, plus a foreign one.
explanation.walkthrough: The ninth letter of the Greek alphabet corresponds to our ninth, I; 'Nine' reads as a count but is a position.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek counterpart of our I, the ninth Greek character, comes from another alphabet.

clue.text: She collects all articles in English

parts.note: the English articles are the indefinite an, the definite the, and the indefinite a
the English articles are the indefinite an, the definite the, and the indefinite a
the English articles are the indefinite an, the definite the, and the indefinite a

explanation.surface: A woman gathers every item in the English collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' suggests items or pieces of writing; they are the grammar words AN, THE and A, run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthea is a woman's name, so stands for a female person.

clue.text: Islander gets a husband, introduced by artist

indicators.note: the artist's name takes the other letters in, introducing them

parts.note: Titian was the Venetian Renaissance painter

explanation.surface: An island woman marries, presented to the painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduced by' puts A and H inside TITIAN after its first T. Gauguin painted Tahitians; Titian is the artist here.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Tahiti in French Polynesia is an inhabitant of that island.
